best_for: Households that want one paid VPN on their Windows PCs, Macs, phones and TV sticks, and who are fine paying for two years up front.

points.title: No free tier
points.text: There is no free plan or trial on the order page. First-time buyers get a 30-day money-back guarantee instead, and the app asks you to sign in before it connects.

points.title: Three plans, priced on a long term
points.text: Basic is listed at USD 2.79 a month, Advanced at USD 3.99 and Express Pro at USD 6.99, each billed as one payment for the first 28 months (USD 78.12, 111.72 and 195.72). After that they renew yearly at USD 99.95, 119.95 and 199.95. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Device count depends on the plan
points.text: Basic covers 10 devices at once, Advanced 12 and Express Pro 14. Count phones, laptops and TVs before you pick a tier.

points.title: What the Windows app gives you
points.text: A kill switch that is on by default, split tunneling, auto-connect rules per network type, a speed test and ExpressVPN's own Lightway protocol. An ad and tracker blocker is included but off until you turn it on, and it only works while connected.

points.title: Windows 10 and 11 only
points.text: The app targets 64-bit Windows 10 and 11, with a separate Arm64 build. Both install machine-wide. Owners of Windows 7 or 8 are pointed to a support article for an older build.

points.title: Mac needs Big Sur or newer
points.text: The Mac app needs macOS 11 or later and runs natively on Apple silicon. The Windows listing here keeps 54 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so a Mac downgrade needs another source.

points.title: Linux exists, just not here
points.text: ExpressVPN publishes a Linux app for Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12, Fedora 39 and Mint 22 or later, plus Arch and 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS. This site lists only the Windows and Mac downloads.
